label: Grace and Works
framing: Grace and works have been pitted against each other for so long that many people no longer know how they fit. Scripture holds both without flinching: we are saved by grace through faith and not by works, and the faith that saves is never alone but always proves itself in a changed life. The tree is not made alive by its fruit, yet a living tree always bears it.
cultural: The early church lived in a world of patron and client, where every gift carried an unpayable obligation, where nothing was ever truly free. Into that economy the gospel announced a gift with no strings, a debt cancelled rather than transferred, and it scandalized everyone. The Greeks heard folly, the religious heard danger, and ordinary people wept, because no one had ever offered them something they could not lose by failing.
historical: Paul and the letter of James, often set against each other, were answering opposite errors: Paul, around AD 50, fighting those who added works to grace, and James, the Lord's brother, fighting those who claimed a faith that never moved a finger to feed the hungry. Dietrich Bonhoeffer, writing from Nazi Germany in 1937, named the counterfeit cheap grace, the grace we bestow on ourselves without repentance, and set against it the costly grace that bids a man come and die.
application: Stop trying to balance grace and works as if they were rivals on a scale. Receive the grace first and entirely, with empty hands, since that is the only way it can be received. Then let the gratitude do what fear never could, serving not to be loved but because you already are. If your obedience feels like a way of buying God, you have not yet believed the gift; if it has vanished altogether, you have not yet received it.

verses.text: For it is by grace you have been saved through faith, and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God, not by works, so that no one can boast.
So too, faith by itself, if it does not result in action, is dead.
For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to everyone. It instructs us to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live sensible, upright, and godly lives in the present age,
For we are God’s workmanship, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance as our way of life.
And if it is by grace, then it is no longer by works. Otherwise, grace would no longer be grace.
